title: Objectwise invariance of homotopy-cartesian squares
statement: Use small simplicial sets, weak homotopy equivalences and homotopy-cartesian squares in the two-leg fibration-replacement sense specified in [lem-coef-kan-fibrant-path-recognition]. Let squares with corners $(Q,X,Y,Z)$ and $(Q^{\prime},X^{\prime},Y^{\prime},Z^{\prime})$ be strictly commutative. Suppose maps $Q\to Q^{\prime}$, $X\to X^{\prime}$, $Y\to Y^{\prime}$, $Z\to Z^{\prime}$ commute with every edge of the squares and are all weak homotopy equivalences. Then the first square is homotopy cartesian if and only if the second square is homotopy cartesian. All eight simplicial sets may be non-Kan or empty.

source.place: Section 2.3, printed p.4, invariance under weak equivalences of squares; in the explicit Kan-replacement/path convention of lem-coef-kan-fibrant-path-recognition. Read online; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy theorem.

proof.text: Choose the functorial fibrant replacement r:S→RS supplied in [lem-coef-kan-fibrant-path-recognition], for each S among Q,X,Y,Z and their primed counterparts. Each component r_S is a trivial cofibration, hence a weak homotopy equivalence in the Kan–Quillen model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core]. For each given corner weak equivalence e:S→S′, naturality gives r_S ≫ R(e)=e ≫ r_{S′}; two-out-of-three therefore makes R(e) a weak equivalence. Functoriality also sends every edge equality of the two strict squares to a strict equality after R. Thus the two R-squares have Kan corners and are connected by an objectwise weak-equivalence map.

source.place: Section 2.3, printed p.4, invariance under weak equivalences; explicit functorial fibrant-replacement reduction in the path convention.

proof.text: Write P=RX×_{RZ,ev₀}Fun(Δ¹,RZ)×_{ev₁,RZ}RY and define P′ analogously. Apply [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] to the cospans RX→RZ←RY and RX′→RZ′←RY′, with comparison maps Rα_X, Rα_Y and Rα_Z. The strict commutation equations from Step 1 are exactly the two hypotheses cu=u′a and cv=v′b of that node, and all six objects are Kan. It follows that the induced map h:P→P′, sending (x,y,γ) to (Rα_X x,Rα_Y y,Rα_Z∘γ), is a weak homotopy equivalence. The formula also shows that h carries the constant path at the common image of a square vertex to the corresponding constant path in the primed square.

source.place: Section 2.3, printed p.4, invariance under weak equivalences of squares, after passing to Kan replacements.

proof.text: Let c:RQ→P and c′:RQ′→P′ be the constant-path comparison maps of [lem-coef-kan-fibrant-path-recognition]. Naturality of R and the coordinate formula for h give the strict equality h∘c=c′∘Rα_Q. By the recognition statement, the first original square is homotopy cartesian exactly when c is a weak homotopy equivalence, and the second exactly when c′ is. Step 1 makes Rα_Q a weak equivalence and Step 2 makes h a weak equivalence. The model two-out-of-three property in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core], applied to this commuting equality, therefore gives c weakly equivalent if and only if c′ is. This proves both directions, including empty or non-Kan original corners, because only their functorial replacements were required.
